title: Recognizing shifted line modules from derived geometric point fibres
statement:
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over a scheme [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, the derived category of module sheaves on its small etale site [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume $E$ is pseudo-coherent and locally bounded below: on each sufficiently small etale affine scheme chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ it corresponds to a pseudo-coherent object of $D(R)$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] whose cohomology vanishes below some integer depending on $U$. Fix $m\in\mathbf Z$. Assume for every geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ that $Lx^*E\simeq\Omega[m]$ in $D(\Omega)$; here $Lx^*$ is derived tensor pullback, so this condition is on derived fibres, not ordinary cohomology fibres. Then $L=H^{-m}(E)$ is a line module on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ and the cohomological truncation comparison is a canonical isomorphism
$$E\simeq L[m]\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_X).$$
A line module means an $\mathcal O_X$-module etale locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Tag 0BYP (lemma-lift-bounded-pseudo-coherent-to-perfect), with ranks d_i=0 except d_{-m}=1; geometric residue extensions detect these ranks. Apply on etale affine charts. The local-ring model is Tag 0BCC (lemma-lift-pseudo-coherent-from-residue-field).

proof.text: Work on one of the sufficiently small etale affine charts $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ in the hypothesis. Let $K\in D(R)$ be its corresponding pseudo-coherent, bounded-below complex, and choose a bounded-above finite-free representative $P^\bullet$. This is precisely the meaning of the chart correspondence in the statement: take associated quasi-coherent sheaves and then their small-etale associated sheaves. [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] gives the affine association, and [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] gives exactness of the second association in the ambient module category. Thus this termwise realization preserves quasi-isomorphisms and computes $E|_U$. For any $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U\to X$ is a geometric point. The finite-free model computes its derived fibre by $P^\bullet\otimes_R\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $Lx^*$ and $Lx_U^*$, for $x_U:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, are computed by applying module pullback to K-flat resolutions with flat terms. Take one, $Q^\bullet\to E$, on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$; its restriction $Q^\bullet|_U$ is K-flat by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat], with flat terms since restriction is exact and commutes with tensor products, and $x^*Q^\bullet=x_U^*(Q^\bullet|_U)$ because $x$ factors through $U$. The realization $\widetilde P^\bullet$ of $P^\bullet$ is bounded above with free terms, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]; it is quasi-isomorphic to $Q^\bullet|_U$, and both compute $Lx_U^*(E|_U)$, so $Lx^*E\simeq x_U^*\widetilde P^\bullet=P^\bullet\otimes_R\Omega$. Consequently the hypothesis says $P^\bullet\otimes_R\Omega\simeq\Omega[m]$.

source.place: Tag 0BYP, lemma-lift-bounded-pseudo-coherent-to-perfect, applied to the affine chart complex; Tag 0BCC explains the residue ranks.

proof.text: Put $C^\bullet=P^\bullet\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Tensor with $\Omega$ is exact, since $\Omega$ is a vector space over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and hence free. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to obtain $H^i(C^\bullet)\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\Omega\cong H^i(C^\bullet\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\Omega)$. The ordinary chain isomorphism $(p\otimes t)\otimes z\mapsto p\otimes tz$, inverse $p\otimes z\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes z$, identifies the right complex with $P^\bullet\otimes_R\Omega$. Every $C^i$ is finite-dimensional, so its subquotient $H^i(C^\bullet)$ is finite-dimensional. A basis of that vector space extends to a basis after tensoring with $\Omega$. The fibre hypothesis therefore gives $d_i=0$ for $i\ne-m$ and $d_{-m}=1$. This uses derived fibres throughout, without identifying them with ordinary fibres of $H^i(K)$.

source.place: Tag 0BYP, lemma-lift-bounded-pseudo-coherent-to-perfect, applied to the affine chart complex; Tag 0BCC explains the residue ranks.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-pseudocoherent-residue-model] to $K$, $\mathfrak p$, and $a=-m$. Its bounded-below hypothesis holds on this chart, and step 2 verifies the residue-cohomology lower bound. It yields $f\notin\mathfrak p$ and a finite-free representative of $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R_f$ whose ranks are the $d_i$. Every term except degree $-m$ is therefore zero, and that term is $R_f$. Both adjacent differentials are zero, so the representative is the one-term complex $R_f[m]$. Hence $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R_f\simeq R_f[m]$. The opens $D(f)$ obtained for all primes cover $U$.

source.place: Tag 0BYP, lemma-lift-bounded-pseudo-coherent-to-perfect, applied to the affine chart complex; Tag 0BCC explains the residue ranks.

proof.text: Realize these one-term models on $D(f)_{\mathrm{et}}$. Restricting the termwise realization of $P^\bullet$ to $D(f)$ gives the termwise realization of $P^\bullet_f=P^\bullet\otimes_RR_f$, since $\widetilde M|_{D(f)}=\widetilde{M_f}$ and the small-etale associated sheaf is computed by pullback to each etale $D(f)$-scheme; and $P^\bullet\otimes_RR_f$ computes $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RR_f$ because $P^\bullet$ is K-flat [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. The affine equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] sends $R_f[m]$ to $\mathcal O_{D(f)}[m]$; the exact comparison [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] sends it to the same one-term structure-sheaf complex on the small etale site. Thus $E|_{D(f)}\simeq\mathcal O_{D(f)}[m]$. Restriction to any object of a localized site is exact on underlying abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact], hence also on module sheaves since kernels and cokernels carry the induced module action. [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^i(E)|_{D(f)}\cong H^i(E|_{D(f)})$. It follows that $H^i(E)|_{D(f)}=0$ for $i\ne-m$, and $H^{-m}(E)|_{D(f)}\cong\mathcal O_{D(f)}$. Taking all these refinements of all affine charts is a covering of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. A sheaf vanishing on this covering vanishes globally: after base change to any object, every section restricts to zero on a cover and is zero by separatedness of the sheaf. Therefore $H^i(E)=0$ for $i\ne-m$, and $L=H^{-m}(E)$ is a line module by its definition.

source.place: Tag 06VE, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits (5), on the small etale site; affine realization Tag 06Z0 and restriction exactness as in sites-modules.tex.

proof.text: Put $r=-m$. Use the canonical truncation comparison $u:\tau_{\le r}E\to E$ and the projection $v:\tau_{\le r}E\to H^r(E)[-r]$ from [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. Step 4 says that $u$ and $v$ induce isomorphisms on every cohomology sheaf: in degree $r$ both induce the identity on $H^r(E)$, and in every other degree all groups are zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] both are isomorphisms in the derived category. Define the comparison to be $v\circ u^{-1}:E\xrightarrow{\sim}H^r(E)[-r]=L[m]$. It is canonical because $u$ and $v$ are the canonical truncation maps; no trivializations of the local line modules are glued or chosen in this comparison.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; two canonical truncation maps when cohomology is supported in degree r.

lean.statement: theorem pseudoCoherent_pointFibre_line {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.SmallModules] [∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] (b : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S), HasDerivedCategory.{wPoint} (schemeSpace (Over.mk b)).SmallModules] (E : X.DerivedModules) (m : ℤ) (hpc : X.IsPseudoCoherent E) (hbelow : ∀ V : X.SmallEtaleModel, ∃ R : Sieve V, R ∈ X.smallEtaleModelTopology V ∧ ∀ (U : X.SmallEtaleModel) (f : U ⟶ V), R f → ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a → IsZero ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor X.smallStructureRings U).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.SmallModules n).obj E))) (hfibre : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (b : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : schemeSpace (Over.mk b) ⟶ X), Nonempty ((derivedTensorPullback x).obj E ≅ (schemeSpace (Over.mk b)).derivedStructure⟦m⟧)) : X.IsLineModule (X.smallModuleEquivalence.inverse.obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.SmallModules (-m)).obj E)) ∧ Nonempty (E ≅ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.SmallModules 0).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.SmallModules (-m)).obj E))⟦m⟧) ∧ ∀ P : CochainComplex X.SmallModules ℤ, Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ E) → IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map (P.ιTruncLE (-m))) ∧ ∃! j : P.truncLE (-m) ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.SmallModules (-m)).obj (P.homology (-m)), j.f (-m) ≫ (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) (-m) (P.homology (-m))).hom = (P.truncLEXIsoCycles (-m)).hom ≫ P.homologyπ (-m) ∧ IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map j)
